dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Rosa. How can I help you?

Hello, yes. Good afternoon. My name is Anabela Fortes. I am calling for my mother, because she is not so comfortable on the phone. Her dog is missing, and I would like to register a lost dog poster. I think this is the right office? I was not sure, so I called the clerk.
You're in the right place to start. Animal control questions come through here, and I can point you to the right people. Let me get some details. When did the dog go missing?

Saturday evening, around six. So, two days now. My mother let him out in the yard, the gate was not latched properly, and he was gone. I am worried because it was very cold on Saturday night, and he is old, eleven years.
I'm sorry, that's stressful. What kind of dog is he?

A beagle mix, brown and white, with one ear that is a little bit folded. His name is Pico. He has a blue collar with a tag, but the tag has an old phone number, so this is a problem. That is why I put my number on the poster.
Okay. And where was he last seen?

At the house. It is 204 Bellevue Avenue. A neighbor thinks she saw him going toward the, um, the side street, but she was not sure. [pause] Sorry, one moment. My brother is texting me again. He texts me the whole time I am talking, I am on speakerphone, so it keeps making noise.
No problem, take your time.
He says, did you call yet. I am calling right now, so, yes. I will answer him later. Okay. I am back.
Sounds like he's worried too. So, for the poster, are you looking to put it up around the neighborhood, or do you want it on file with the city?

Both, if possible. I made a poster already, with the photo, and the description. I want to register it so that if somebody finds him and calls the city, there is a record. Also I want to ask, who responds? If someone calls about a dog found on the street, who comes? Is it police, or somebody different?
It's the animal control officer who handles stray and found dogs. After hours the police dispatch can reach them. So if someone calls in a found beagle, they'd check against reports like yours.
Okay. So the officer, not the police directly. That is good to know. And the officer can call me, on this number, if the dog is found?
Yes, that's what we'd put on the report. Can I confirm your number? Go ahead.
Yes. It is four zero one, five five five, zero one five five.
Four oh one, five five five, oh one five five. Got it. And the name on the report, is it you or your mother?
Put my mother as the owner, but me as the contact. Her name is the same as mine, Fortes, but the first name is different. Wait, [line breaks up] can you hear me? The phone is making a noise.
I lost you for a second. Say that again, the last part.
The owner is my mother, Fortes, and I am the contact person. I will spell. F, O, R, T, E, S.
Perfect. I'll note you as the contact. And I'm going to ask, does Pico have a microchip?
Yes, he does. He got it at the vet, maybe six years ago. I do not have the number with me, but the vet has it. Should I bring it?

If you can get it from the vet, great, and call back or give it to the animal control officer. It helps a lot if he's scanned. Also check with the local shelters and vets in case someone dropped him off.

Yes, I did call two vets already this morning. Nothing yet. [pause] Sorry. My brother again. He says maybe we should walk the cliff path. I told him, the path is long, and it is cold, and my mother cannot go. But he can go. He is going to go.
That's a good idea, someone should walk the area. Dogs often stay close to where they got out, or they follow a scent trail. Calling out to him helps too.
Okay. And about the poster itself. Is there some rule where I can put it? I do not want to do something wrong, like put it on a pole where it is not allowed.

For that, I don't have a list in front of me. Lost pet flyers are common, but if you want to be sure about poles and public boards, I can have someone from the department call you back. Otherwise, shops and community boards are usually fine if you ask.
I would like the call back, please, if it is easy. Not only for the poles. I would also like to ask what else the officer can do, for example if they drive around, or if they have a list.
I'll put that in the message. Questions about poles and what the officer can do for a missing dog. Same number, the oh one five five one?
Yes, same number. The best time is after four, because I am working until then. But if they call earlier I will answer anyway. I have the phone next to me.
Got it. I'll mark after four preferred. And the report is for a beagle mix named Pico, brown and white, folded ear, blue collar, last seen Saturday around six at 204 Bellevue Avenue. Is that right?
Yes, correct. Eleven years old. Also, he is a little bit deaf, so if someone calls him he might not respond. I should say this, maybe it is important.
That is important. I'll add that he's hard of hearing, and that he may not come when called. People should approach slowly.
Thank you. This is good. I was thinking that nobody would take it seriously because he is only a dog, but you are very kind.
Of course. He's family. Do you want me to also note that your mother is at the house, in case someone drops by with him?

Yes, please. She is home most of the day. She will open the door, but she speaks only a little English, so if somebody comes, she may need to call me. [pause] Okay, my brother wrote again. He says he found a different poster of a lost cat on the pole, so maybe that area is fine. I will tell him to wait for the answer.
Good idea, hold off until you hear back. I'll get this to the right person right away.
Thank you very much. So, to repeat, someone calls me after four, the animal control officer is the one who responds, and I should bring the microchip number when I have it.
That's it exactly. And call us if he turns up so we can close out the report.
Yes, I will. Thank you, Rosa. Goodbye.
Goodbye, and I hope Pico's home soon.
